title: Tenant-phased abort and live-fix protocol for mixed deployment rollouts
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Issue: Recent model rollout produced non-deterministic regressions observed only for a subset of tenants across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Root cause appears to be a combination of kernel scheduling change + KV cache invalidation race when slice traffic is moved between backends. Goal: create an operational protocol that enables interruptible, tenant-phased aborts, live-patch hotfix injection, and deterministic KV-cache reconciliation while minimizing blast radius and providing clear customer communication pathways.
success_criteria: 1) Ability to quarantine affected tenant slices within 3 minutes of alert; 2) Deterministic KV cache reconciliation that prevents stale context for >99.9% of requests post-rollback; 3) Live patch (non-disruptive hotfix) can be applied to a canary subset without changing routing for unaffected tenants; 4) Customer-facing SLA notification and mitigation steps documented and templated; 5) Postmortem with action items and regression test added to CI within 5 business days.
runbook_steps: Detect: automated anomaly detection flags sudden quality delta + latency spike on route X; on-call confirms tenant list and percent traffic affected.
Quarantine: flip header-based slice routing to quarantine pool (zeroing new model variant traffic) for affected tenants; leave unaffected tenants on original route.
Snapshot: capture live KV cache digests and sequence numbers for affected hosts; persist to durable store for reconciliation.
Isolate: if quarantine fails or error rate stays above threshold, perform tenant-phased abort: revert only affected tenant routing to previous model variant while keeping global rollout unchanged.
Live-fix: if a deterministic small patch is available (e.g., kernel pin, config toggle), apply hotpatch agent to canary hosts; verify end-to-end for 1000 sample requests before wider rollout.
KV reconciliation: apply reconcile job that replays a prefix of requests against old/new caches using captured digests; validate outputs for drift and apply cache repair per-host.
Communication: trigger templated customer notification (Support -> customer -> account SLA) and create a status page update; PM/SE to open dedicated customer bridge if high-impact.
Rollforward/Rollback: after validation, either roll forward corrected variant with staged traffic or fully rollback across all tenants with coordinated KV cache flush and idempotent reconciliation.
Postmortem: gather logs, model diffs, kernel telemetry; perform RCA and schedule regression tests and release gating updates.
rollback_playbook_summary: A tenant-phased rollback that uses header-sliced routing to move only impacted tenant traffic back to the last-known-good variant, followed by KV cache reconciliation and optional live-patch. The playbook prioritizes preserving unaffected tenant performance and minimizing cross-deployment cascade by avoiding blanket rollback unless evidence suggests global corruption.
decisions: Prefer tenant-phased aborts over global rollbacks by default for mixed deployments to reduce blast radius.
Require KV cache snapshot before any routing changes for rollouts touching stateful caches.
Hotpatches permitted only if they are <= 5 LOC runtime toggles or kernel config flips and pass a 1-hour canary acceptance window.
Customer communication must be owned by SE/PM for P0 incidents and use pre-approved templates in /confluence/rollouts/safety.
